relations.subject: John Chadwick
relations.evidence: After the end of the war in 1945, he returned to his studies at Cambridge, graduating with First Class Honours in Classics Part II, with a distinction in his special subject, linguistics.

relations.subject: John Chadwick
relations.evidence: In 1950 he published his first scholarly work, an edition of The Medical Works of Hippocrates, co-authored with his cousin, William Neville Mann, a distinguished physician.

relations.subject: John Chadwick
relations.evidence: After finishing his degree, he joined the staff of the Oxford Latin Dictionary before beginning a Classics lectureship at Cambridge in 1952.

relations.subject: John Chadwick
relations.role: Perceval Maitland Laurence Reader in Classics
relations.evidence: He retired in 1984, by which time he had become the fourth (and last) Perceval Maitland Laurence Reader in Classics at Cambridge.
